questions.stem: A student measures the temperature inside a flask of germinating peas over 24 hours and finds it increases by 3°C. Which statement best explains this observation?

options.text: Photosynthesis in the peas releases heat energy
Aerobic respiration is exothermic and releases energy as heat
Anaerobic respiration produces ethanol which warms the flask
The peas absorb heat from the surroundings during germination

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration is an exothermic reaction — glucose is broken down using oxygen, and some of the energy released is transferred as heat to the surroundings. Germinating peas respire rapidly, which is why the temperature rises.

questions.stem: A doctor explains to a patient that their muscle cells need a constant supply of glucose and oxygen. What are the products of the reaction that uses these substances in the cells?

options.text: Lactic acid and energy
Carbon dioxide and water
Ethanol and carbon dioxide
Water and oxygen

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration uses glucose and oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. Energy is also transferred, but the chemical products are CO₂ and H₂O.

questions.stem: An athlete's breathing rate and heart rate both increase during a 10 km run. How does this support aerobic respiration in the muscles?

options.text: It removes lactic acid from the muscles more quickly
It delivers more glucose and oxygen to muscle cells and removes CO₂ faster
It increases the temperature of the blood to speed up respiration
It converts anaerobic respiration into aerobic respiration in the lungs

questions.explanation: Faster breathing increases gas exchange (more O₂ in, more CO₂ out), and a higher heart rate delivers oxygenated blood to muscles more rapidly. This ensures aerobic respiration can continue to meet the increased energy demand.

questions.stem: A biologist places a living organism in a sealed container with a carbon dioxide probe. Over one hour, the CO₂ concentration rises steadily. Which conclusion is most justified?

options.text: The organism is carrying out photosynthesis
The organism is dead and decomposing
The organism is carrying out aerobic respiration
The container must contain anaerobic conditions

questions.explanation: A steady rise in CO₂ indicates the organism is respiring — aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide as a waste product. If the organism were photosynthesising, CO₂ levels would fall. The organism is described as living, so decomposition is not the best answer.

questions.stem: A hospital patient is given supplemental oxygen through a mask. Why would cells that receive more oxygen be able to release more energy?

options.text: Oxygen is a source of chemical energy that cells can use directly
Oxygen speeds up anaerobic respiration in the cells
Oxygen is needed as a reactant in aerobic respiration to fully break down glucose
Oxygen combines with lactic acid to form ATP

questions.explanation: Oxygen is a reactant in aerobic respiration. With more oxygen available, cells can carry out aerobic respiration more effectively, fully breaking down glucose to release much more energy per molecule than anaerobic respiration would.
